question: Indicate which serum biochemical profile is suggestive of rickets due to vitamin D deficiency in a 5-month-old infant:

options.opa: Normal calcium; normal phosphate; normal alkaline phosphatases (FA); normal parathyroid hormone (PTH); 25 OH vitamin D low.
options.opb: Normal calcium; low phosphate; Normal FA; Normal PTH; 25 OH vitamin D low.
options.opc: Low calcium; high phosphate; FA elevated; Normal PTH; 25 OH vitamin D low.
options.opd: Normal calcium; normal phosphate; FA elevated; Elevated PTH; 25 OH vitamin D low.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Vitamin D deficiency" -> "decreased intestinal absorption of calcium" -> "normal serum calcium levels" -> "normal serum phosphate levels" -> "normal alkaline phosphatase levels" -> "elevated parathyroid hormone" -> "low 25 OH vitamin D" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Vitamin D deficiency" -> "increased bone resorption" -> "low serum calcium" -> "high serum phosphate" -> "elevated alkaline phosphatase" -> "normal parathyroid hormone" -> "low 25 OH vitamin D" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Vitamin D deficiency" -> "increased parathyroid hormone secretion" -> "normal serum calcium" -> "low serum phosphate" -> "normal alkaline phosphatase" -> "low 25 OH vitamin D" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Vitamin D deficiency" -> "increased bone turnover" -> "normal serum calcium" -> "normal phosphate" -> "elevated alkaline phosphatase" -> "elevated parathyroid hormone" -> "low 25 OH vitamin D" -> 75%
analysis: Rickets due to vitamin D deficiency typically presents with low serum calcium, low phosphate, elevated alkaline phosphatase (FA), and elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels. In this case, the option that aligns with these findings is option 'opd', which indicates normal calcium and phosphate but elevated FA and PTH, along with low 25 OH vitamin D, suggesting a compensatory response to low vitamin D levels.
